references.text: The instructions that the priests shall eat the sin offering in a holy place, as Moses refers to in his rebuke of Aaron and his sons.
The provision that all male priests may eat from the sin offering, and that it is most holy.
The laws concerning the sin offering (חַטָּאת) which Moses refers to when he asks why they did not eat it.
The concept of bearing (לָשֵׂאת) the people's sins to make atonement, also seen in the ritual of the scapegoat.
Aaron bears the guilt (עָוֺן) associated with the holy gifts, similar to the concept of bearing the congregation's sin.
Aaron and his sons shall bear the guilt connected to the sanctuary, parallel to bearing the congregation's sin.
The Lord's suffering servant bears (יִשָּׂא) many sins and makes atonement, a prophetic parallel to the priest's role.
The offering that makes atonement (לְכַפֵּר) for the people, with the same purpose as the sin offering in Leviticus.
Christ was offered once to bear many sins, fulfilling the priest's role with the sin offering.
Christ bore our sins in his body, the ultimate fulfillment of bearing the people's sin for atonement.
